subject: MSA — governing law & injunctive relief carve (SeedBridge)
messages:
From: Maya Kapoor <maya.kapoor@seedbridge.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: Rafael Ortega <rafael.ortega@seedbridge.com>, SeedBridge Legal <legal@seedbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Draft MSA - governing law and injunctive relief

Hi Irene,

Thanks for sending the draft. Our legal team reviewed the MSA and pushed a couple of blocks: they want California substantive law and courts for disputes. They also requested that arbitration be removed from the agreement in favor of court litigation (they're concerned about discovery limitations in arbitration for life sciences contracts).

Two specific asks from SeedBridge Legal:
- Governing law: California (they are headquartered in SF)
- No arbitration; disputes to be resolved in state or federal court in California

That said, they are willing to accept an equitable relief carve if Redwood insists on arbitration for most disputes — SeedBridge wants clear language that injunctive relief (for IP/data misuse) can be brought in California courts without having to clear arbitration first.

I attached our redline (MSA_Redline_SeedBridge_20260929.docx). Can your legal team confirm whether Redwood can accept: (a) California law & courts for injunctive relief only, with arbitration for other disputes; or (b) propose a compromise jurisdiction?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement team is trying to get the PO over the line this week.

Best,
Maya Kapoor
Head of Partnerships
SeedBridge

Attachment: MSA_Redline_SeedBridge_20260929.docx (Word doc, 62KB)

From: irene.choi@redwood.com <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Maya Kapoor <maya.kapoor@seedbridge.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Draft MSA - governing law and injunctive relief

Hi Maya — thanks for the redline and context. Looping in Laura (legal) and Aditya (commercial) to align. Quick answers up front: we are reluctant to accept general California law + courts for all disputes because the broader platform SLAs and enterprise contracts are governed under Delaware, which gives us predictability across customers. We can, however, be flexible around emergency equitable relief.

Proposed compromise for your team to consider:
- Governing law: Delaware (without affecting choice of venue for temporary remedies)
- Dispute resolution: binding arbitration (commercial arbitration rules) for all disputes EXCEPT that either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction in California (SeedBridge's headquarters) prior to or during arbitration to preserve rights or prevent data/IP misuse.

Concrete clause suggestion we can put into the next redline:
"Notwithstanding Section X (Arbitration), either party may seek interim injunctive relief or other provisional remedies in the state or federal courts sitting in the State of California to protect confidential information, intellectual property rights, or to prevent imminent harm, provided that such relief shall not modify the parties' agreement to arbitrate the merits of any dispute."

If that sounds reasonable we can produce an edit and send back for your counsel to review. If SeedBridge insists on full litigation in California courts for all disputes, we will need a commercial escalation (Aditya and I to review pricing/SLA tradeoffs).

Irene Choi
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: OrderForm_v3.pdf (PDF stub)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA - governing law & injunctive relief (internal)

Irene / Aditya — see my notes for the compromise and fallback language. I support the carve for provisional remedies in California courts but we should tighten the scope: limit to (i) injunctive relief to protect IP and confidential data, (ii) preservation of evidence, and (iii) urgent preservation of service continuity (e.g., immediate suspension/termination requests that can't wait). Also add a clause stating that any court action for provisional relief shall be without prejudice to arbitration and shall not be used to circumvent arbitration discovery limits.

Suggested redline text (short form):
"Notwithstanding Section X (Arbitration), either party may seek interim injunctive relief or other provisional remedies in the state or federal courts located in the County of San Francisco, State of California, solely to the extent necessary to preserve rights relating to: (a) protection of intellectual property; (b) protection of confidential information; and (c) urgent measures to preserve service continuity. Any such action shall be without prejudice to, and shall not be deemed a waiver of, the obligation of the parties to arbitrate the merits of the dispute."

If SeedBridge pushes for California substantive law for all disputes, recommend the following commercial-level responses: 1) escalate to commercial leadership for contract concession sign-off, 2) offer a mutual waiver of jury trial and agree to venue in California but keep governing law as Delaware, or 3) offer a single exception: California law only for the Order Form and any SOWs where necessary (limited application).

I'll prepare a marked-up MSA with the provisional remedy carve and send it back to Maya.

- Laura
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Maya Kapoor <maya.kapoor@seedbridge.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: Rafael Ortega <rafael.ortega@seedbridge.com>, legal@seedbridge.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA — governing law & injunctive relief carve (SeedBridge)

Irene / Laura / Aditya — thanks for the swift review and the proposed text. SeedBridge Legal is comfortable with the narrow provisional relief carve you proposed, provided two small edits: (1) specify "County of San Francisco" as the venue for injunctive relief; and (2) add a 14-day meet-and-confer requirement before either party seeks injunctive relief, except that the meet-and-confer requirement will not apply where immediate relief is required to avoid irreparable harm.

We attached a one-line edit in the Doc (see link) and our procurement team is standing by to complete the PO after we get the updated MSA. If you can upload the revised MSA to DocuSign (https://docusign.com/seedbridge/sb-092-msa) with that carve, we'll start signatures today.

Thanks — looking forward to closing.

Best,
Maya
Head of Partnerships
SeedBridge
